chapter: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
title: Benny Carter's band at the Savoy and the 1941 record
summary: Carter's refined band was too polished for jitterbug dancers, who preferred the Savoy Sultans and Erskine Hawkins, so work was irregular.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: But getting back to 1940 and well, you recorded then in '41, I know with Benny Carter, Vic Dickenson, Archy Archie, Sidney Sydney DeParis and I think Maxine Sullivan was the vocalist, I guess she was big then?
And -- so that was then -- were you with the Benny Carter band at the time you recorded in '41?
Yes, we were at the Savoy.
I see so you joined him in 1940, but you -- you were still with him in April?

Yes, we didn't stay too long up there with the band, because the work was very -- you know at that time they would like hire one week-end then maybe after a couple of weeks, we'd go up there for another couple days, something like that, because it wasn't regular. They didn't keep any band up there, that type, you know, any length of time. Cause they were more interested in bands like the Savoy Sultans, they stayed up there, because the people were jumping more to that type of band, than they were Benny Carter's band. Benny Carter's band was a little too refined for the jitterbug dancers.
So they liked a band like the Sultans and Erskine Hawkins, type of band came and stayed there.
